newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol night freighter ban may face legal action.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol night freighter ban may face legal action.

text.p: Aero Groundservices B.V.(AGS) said it may take legal action against Amsterdam Schiphol Airport concerning a night take-off ban to be introduced on some freighter aircraft from August 1.
AGS is Schiphol's largest air cargo handling company and managing director, Frans Goudsmit told Reuters: "We are considering what steps we will take but we have not excluded legal action."
He added that the company is not alone in considering such steps.
Separately KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV has described the restrictions as: "unacceptable, both operationally and commercially".

Schiphol announced on Friday that McDonnell Douglas DC-10 aircraft and the Boeing 747 in its 100, 200, 300 and SP versions cannot take-off between 2300 hours and 0600 hours from August 1 in a bid to reduce noise pollution at the airport.
The airport authority's proposal is now subject to approval of the Dutch government.
AGS handles El Al and U.S.-based Polar Air which are among the carriers that have been hit most by Schiphol's unexpected announcement.
Goudsmit said: "Perhaps some of the carriers can reschedule their flights but if they consider more serious action such as moving their freight hub, AGS will be very badly effected."
Goudsmit estimated that 2,000 freighter flights a year are handled by his company and around half of these are night flights.
He added that this ban could also put jobs in jeopardy as of the 1,000 people employed at the company, 400 are dedicated to handling cargo aircraft.
One of AGS' major customers El Al, which has called at the airport for 40 years, has already said that it may be forced to consider moving its freighter hub.
Goudsmit questioned the effect of the move on Schiphol's position as a leading freight airport.
He was also concerned at the potential impact it will have on the Aalsmeer flower auction as many of the carriers hit by the ban also transport flowers and some of the fly during the night.
